Kernel `fold_finish_1` · **UNVERIFIED** · [all operations](index.md) · [how to read this page](reading.md)

## What it computes

The result of a fold from its final state $s$: the state itself when its leading limb is finite, with the flag $\mathit{flag}$ true; otherwise a NaN in every limb and the flag false (the canonical NaN of [When something is not finite](../developer/design/milestone2.md#sum-dot-axpy-convolution)):

$$r = s \ \text{when } s_0 \text{ is finite}, \qquad r = \mathrm{NaN} \text{ otherwise}.$$

## C++

No public operation computes this kernel on its own.

## Requires

- $s$ is any value of `T`: a number, $\pm\infty$ or a NaN.

## Target (not proved)

For operands that satisfy the requirements, finite, infinite or NaN:

- $\mathit{flag}$ is true exactly when $s$ is finite.
- When it is, $r = s$, limb for limb.
- Otherwise every limb of $r$ is a NaN.

Stated for every binary format with a precision of at least 1 bit, rounding to nearest with ties to even and with gradual underflow, in the IEEE model, with signed zeros, infinities, NaN and overflow. Both limb types qualify: `double` has 53 bits, `float` has 24 bits.

## Listing

From [`gen/kernels/fold_finish_1.kernel`](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/blob/main/gen/kernels/fold_finish_1.kernel), the description the C++ and the formal model (`proofs/gen/IeeeModel.v`) are generated from. Each line is one operation of `T`; one that rounds rounds to nearest, and `prod(a, b)` is $\mathrm{RN}(ab)$, written as a fused multiply-add with a zero addend ([the kernel IR](../developer/architecture.md#the-kernel-ir)).

```
# The finish of a fold of one limb (milestone2.md, "When something is not finite"): the final
# state when it is finite, with the flag true; otherwise the canonical NaN and the flag false.
# Which infinity an IEEE sum of the operands would have given is not computed: D5's "not finite,
# which value is unspecified", made a definite value.

a    = abs(s)
flag = lt(a, const inf)
r    = select(flag, s, const nan)
```
